topic: Outage Files: ransomware takes IDCF Cloud East Japan Region 1 offline (495 customers), vs physical causes in the incident database

sources.title: Ransomware attack disrupts Japan's IDCF Cloud used by govt clients
facts: The attack started on October 7 at 3:40 AM local time, forcing a shutdown of the network and system
IDC Frontier (a SoftBank Group subsidiary) said a disruption in East Japan Region 1 was caused by a ransomware attack by a third party
The attack impacts 495 companies and local governments using its cloud service
IDC Frontier isolated and shut down impacted systems in East Japan Region 1; IDCF Cloud disabled customer access to management consoles for all regions
The company is working to identify and block the intrusion route and check security in other regions

sources.title: SoftBank national cloud arm attacked in 'seven minutes,' taking Japan infrastructure offline
facts: Virtual servers in four availability zones had stopped and could not restart
IDC Frontier said it would be difficult to retrieve or restore customer data from the affected infrastructure; customers may have to restore from their own backups
Customer notice: 'we are advising you to prepare a separate environment and rebuild your system'
141 incidents logged since 2015; 35 of them in 2026
By cause: power 32; fire 28; cooling 25; weather 7; flood/water 6; fire suppression 6; grid 2; software 2; other 2; no published cause 31
The IDC Frontier ransomware attack (7 Oct 2026) is filed under cause 'other'

caption:
495 companies and local governments were on the cloud region a ransomware attack took offline on 7 Oct.

The attack on IDC Frontier's IDCF Cloud began at 3:40 AM local time. The company isolated East Japan Region 1, virtual servers in four zones stopped, and customers were told their data may be difficult to recover.

Most incidents in our database are physical: power (32), fire (28), cooling (25). Cyber events are rare there, but this one took out a whole region.

Sources: BleepingComputer (8 Oct), SDxCentral (9 Oct), Coloprice incident database. Details on the last slide.
